content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

Question: progressive_late_moov.mp4 takes forever to start on my phone when i use mobile data, once it starts it plays fine. why is it so slow to start??

Findings:
- media: Findings: ffprobe confirms the late moov: progressive_late_moov.mp4 has "mp4_top_level_boxes": ["ftyp", "free", "mdat", "moov"], so `moov` comes after `mdat` (h264 High 1280x720 30 fps plus aac LC, 2.0 s, both start_time 0.000000); [kb:mp4-faststart] explains why this slows startup: the `moov` index is often written at the end, so "a progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests", which fits slow start on mobile data but smooth playback afterwards; fix: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`, then re-check box order (expect moov before mdat); for adaptive streaming the KB prefers fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS).

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}]}

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}]}

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}]}

{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:

  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}, {"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}]}

same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}]}

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}]}

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.

  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.

User suspects the moov atom is late in the file so first range requests stall. {"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:

- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

Question: On a device in the field, Widevine appears to resolve to L3 and caps us at SD. Is there a supported runtime check for the DRM security level, such as the MediaDrm securityLevel property, and what should we expect to see on an L3 device before we request the license?

Findings:
- knowledge: Findings: Yes, [kb:widevine-levels] documents a runtime check: read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`; it explains that Widevine has L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted environment) and L3 (software only), that "content owners commonly restrict HD and higher renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device", and that a device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or failed keybox provisioning, after which "the license server then refuses HD keys"; the KB does not describe any step that lets an L3 device obtain HD keys before the license request, so the expectation is to read the level first, cap the requested tier at SD on L3, and log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a network or provisioning error; the KB has nothing device-specific because no model was given.

messages.content: Brief from the planner: User asks how to make progressive MP4 videos start faster (long time to first frame on phones). No file or device named. Please answer from the knowledge base: server-side changes (e.g. moov at the front, faststart, range request support) and player-side changes (buffering thresholds).

content.text: Searching the knowledge base for faster progressive MP4 startup.

input.query: progressive MP4 faster start moov front faststart range requests buffering thresholds

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}]}

content.text: Checking the KB on HDR10 surface configuration and flat/grey output.

input.query: HDR10 washed out flat grey Surface colour space SurfaceView TextureView tone mapping

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.
- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer
  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or
  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

Question: Progressive mp4 playback is slow to start on some CDN edges while others are fine. What should I check first: the moov atom position, the initial buffer thresholds, or the range request behaviour?

Findings:
- knowledge: Findings: From the KB, check moov atom position first: [kb:mp4-faststart] says that with `moov` at the end of the file "a progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests"; check which atom comes first with `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` and remux with `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4` if moov is last; the KB has no entry on initial buffer thresholds, CDN edge behaviour or range request handling by servers, so it cannot explain why only some edges are slow; since moov position is a property of the file, a difference between edges would suggest comparing the files and range-request responses served by each edge, but that is my inference, not something the KB states.

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "behind-live-window", "title": "BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams", "text": "# BehindLiveWindowException in Media3 / ExoPlayer live streams

A live stream exposes a sliding window of segments. If playback falls further behind than
the window (long pause, slow network, app in the background), the segments it needs are gone
and the player raises a `BehindLiveWindowException`, surfaced as a `PlaybackException` with
error code `ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW`.

Fix: in `Player.Listener.onPlayerError`, check for that error code, then call
`player.seekToDefaultPosition()` followed by `player.prepare()` to rejoin at the live edge.
Consider a longer live window on the server or a smaller target live offset on the client."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

Question: Since lumen-l3 has a hardware AV1 decoder, av1_2160p60.mkv should go through the c2 hardware AV1 decoder without falling back to software. What is the cleanest way to request that codec explicitly, and how do I confirm in our track selector that the 2160p60 profile is actually hardware-backed?

Findings:
- media: Findings: ffprobe on av1_2160p60.mkv reports codec av1, "profile": "Main", 3840x2160, "avg_frame_rate": "60/1", "pix_fmt": "yuv420p" (a level is not reported); I have no codec_caps tool and the KB has no lumen-l3 entry, so whether lumen-l3 has a hardware AV1 decoder and whether it supports 2160p60 is not verified here and the user's hardware assumption is unconfirmed (the device specialist should run codec_caps on lumen-l3 for video/av01); [kb:av1-decoding] says Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) from API 29, that "hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version", and that software decoding "can be too slow for high resolutions or frame rates"; to confirm hardware backing the KB says to enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for `video/av01`, use `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+, and check `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` for sizes and frame rates, falling back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed; the KB does not cover requesting a codec by name (e.g. createByCodecName), so I cannot state that procedure from the evidence.
- device: Findings: The user's assumption is wrong: codec_caps for lumen-l3 (video/av01, "android_api_level": 33) lists only one AV1 decoder, `c2.android.av1.decoder` with "hardware": false (software), profile "Main", "max_width": 1920, "max_height": 1080 and "max_fps_at_max_size": 30, so lumen-l3 has no hardware AV1 decoder and does not support 2160p60: the clip av1_2160p60.mkv is AV1 Main, 3840x2160 at 60 fps per the earlier ffprobe, which is four times the pixels and double the frame rate of the decoder's listed limit; this agrees with [kb:av1-decoding] that hardware AV1 depends on the SoC and software AV1 "can be too slow for high resolutions or frame rates", and the fix suggested there is to check `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` and fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC (or serve a 1080p30-or-lower AV1 rendition); since only one AV1 decoder exists, requesting a codec by name would not yield a hardware one, and confirming hardware backing on the device uses `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+, which here should return false for `c2.android.av1.decoder`; the evidence does not cover how to request a codec by name.

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:
- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).
- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason
  HDR output gets flattened.

  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.
- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or

11-20 14:02:11.309  8123  8194 E CCodec  : Failed to create component: c2.lumen.avc.decoder (NO_MEMORY: max instances reached)
11-20 14:02:11.310  8123  8194 E MediaCodec: Codec reported err 0xfffffff4/NO_MEMORY, actionCode 0, while in state 1/ALLOCATING
11-20 14:02:11.312  8123  8123 E ThumbGrid: decoder init failed for position=4
11-20 14:02:11.312  8123  8123 E ThumbGrid: android.media.MediaCodec$CodecException: Failed to initialize c2.lumen.avc.decoder, error 0xfffffff4

Findings:
- device: Findings: The log shows decoder exhaustion: logcat_grep (17 matches) shows c2.lumen.avc.decoder allocated once per bound item for positions 0-3 (L2, L4, L6, L8), then at position 4 "L11: 11-20 14:02:11.309 ... E CCodec : Failed to create component: c2.lumen.avc.decoder (NO_MEMORY: max instances reached)", "L12: ... Codec reported err 0xfffffff4/NO_MEMORY ... while in state 1/ALLOCATING", and "L13/L14: ... ThumbGrid: decoder init failed for position=4 ... CodecException: Failed to initialize c2.lumen.avc.decoder, error 0xfffffff4"; codec_caps for lumen-l3 reports "max_concurrent_hw_video_decoders": 4 for the hardware c2.lumen.avc.decoder, so the fifth allocation (position 4) is the first one past the limit, matching the log; further evidence of a leak is "L17: 11-20 14:02:11.390 ... W ThumbGrid: recycled position=0 but decoder not released", and the failure repeats for position 5 (L16); codec_caps reports a device-wide hardware decoder count, not a per-component instance limit, but the two agree on 4 here, and I did not search the KB; the evidence supports releasing decoders when items are recycled or limiting concurrent thumbnail decoders to 4 or fewer.

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "audio-focus", "title": "Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)", "text": "# Audio keeps playing over calls or other apps (audio focus)

Android coordinates audio between apps with audio focus. An app that never requests focus,
or ignores focus loss, keeps playing over navigation prompts, calls, or other media.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to
  `ExoPlayer.setAudioAttributes(...)`; the player then requests focus, ducks, and pauses for you.
- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.
- Also handle `ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY` to pause when headphones are unplugged."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.

Fix:
- With Media3, pass suitable `AudioAttributes` and `handleAudioFocus = true` to

- Without Media3, request focus with an `AudioFocusRequest` (API 26+) and react to
  `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS`, `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, and `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT_CAN_DUCK`.

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;

- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}

{"results": [{"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}

function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.

Checks:

  HDR output gets flattened.

  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.

  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}]}

messages.content:
Brief from the planner: On one test phone (device id not given) only SD comes from the DRM session although the license response reports L1; MediaDrm getPropertyString securityLevel returns L3 on that device. Question: is the resolution cap gated on HDCP level or OEM CDM build, and what in the license request decides the cap with DefaultDrmSessionManager. Check the device's Widevine level via codec_caps and the KB on Widevine security level/resolution caps.

Findings so far:
- device: Findings: The device id is unknown so I did not run codec_caps; the evidence is the planner's own report that `MediaDrm getPropertyString("securityLevel")` returns L3 on that phone, which [kb:widevine-levels] treats as the thing that matters for HD: Widevine L3 is software only and "content owners commonly restrict HD and higher renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device", and a device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox provisioning, after which "the license server then refuses HD keys"; so a license response that says L1 conflicts with the device-reported L3, and the KB suggests logging the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal from a network or provisioning error; the KB says nothing about HDCP levels, OEM CDM builds or `DefaultDrmSessionManager` request parameters, so whether the cap is gated on HDCP or the CDM build and what in the request decides it is not established by the evidence.

content.text: Searching the KB for Widevine security level and resolution caps.

content.content:
{"results": [{"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel")`.
- A device can drop from L1 to L3 after an unlocked bootloader or a failed keybox
  provisioning; the license server then refuses HD keys.
- Log the license request and response status to tell a policy refusal apart from a
  network or provisioning error."}, {"id": "mediacodec-errors", "title": "MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures", "text": "# MediaCodec.CodecException and configure failures

`MediaCodec.CodecException` reports whether an error is transient (`isTransient()`: retry the
same call later) or recoverable (`isRecoverable()`: call `stop()`, `configure()`, `start()`
again). Anything else means releasing the codec and creating a new one.

Common causes:
- The format, profile, or level is not supported by any decoder on the device. Query
  `MediaCodecList` and `MediaCodecInfo.CodecCapabilities` before configuring.
- Too many codec instances are alive at once. Hardware codecs are a shared, limited resource;
  release codecs you no longer use.
- The output `Surface` was released while the codec still used it.

Log the `diagnosticInfo` string from the exception; it names the failing component."}]}
